first.rationale: Targeted promotional pricing most directly counters SMB losses and has prior acquisition and revenue lift, but its effects on customer quality, retention, and post-promotion revenue need verification. Onboarding simplification is the strongest alternative given the completion and activation declines, so its source should also be checked before committing.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified evidence shows higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Reject promotional pricing this cycle because its verified 12% retention decline undermines long-term value despite near-term revenue lift.

final2.rationale: Continue with shortened onboarding. The intensified pricing threat raises urgency but does not overturn verified evidence: the prior 40% SMB discount increased acquisition while reducing 30-day retention by 12%, making promotional pricing inconsistent with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Shortened onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and retention, directly addressing current operational declines. The competitor’s deeper cut may change market dynamics, but without new verification it is not sufficient to adopt a strategy already shown to damage cohort survival.
